c.tagline: Seljuk Anatolia at the foot of Mount Erciyes — pastırma, citadel bazaars and the road to Cappadocia.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; hailing via the BiTaksi app (or Uber, which dispatches licensed taxis) avoids fare disputes.

emergency.note: 112 is Türkiye's single emergency number for ambulance, fire and police.

hood_desc: The historic core around Cumhuriyet Square, dominated by the black-stone Kayseri Castle, the covered bazaar and Seljuk monuments like the Hunat Hatun Complex; the best base for sightseeing on foot.
The main central district spreading south and east of the old city, with modern shopping, parks, hotels and Erciyes University nearby; a convenient, well-connected place to stay.
The western central district around the railway station and business areas, with malls and the Kayseray tram running through; practical and well-served by transit.
A historic hillside town, now a leafy university suburb east of the center, known for restored stone houses, cafés and cooler air; a relaxed, characterful alternative to the city center.
A village-like neighborhood on the lower slopes of Mount Erciyes, the gateway to the Erciyes ski resort; quiet and scenic, best for skiers and mountain trips.

water.note: Tap is treated but most locals drink bottled water.

transit.hours: The Kayseray tram and city buses run roughly 6:00 AM to midnight; taxis and ride apps cover later hours.
transit.note: Kayseri's public transport centers on the Kayseray light-rail tram line crossing the city, backed by an extensive municipal bus network; a single Kart 38 smartcard works across both.
transit.pay: Tram and buses are cashless — you tap a rechargeable Kart 38 smartcard, sold and topped up at stations and kiosks; single fares are inexpensive.

bus: Kayseri Intercity Bus Terminal (regional & national coaches)

transit.m: City bus to the center (~25-30 min)
Taxi to the city center (10-15 min)

tip.r: Around 5-10% at restaurants is customary for good service; leaving it in cash is preferred.
